# Synthetic input: tiny Python CLI

This is a documentation/process fixture, not a real product or claim of a release.
The directory has only this description and `main.py`; there are no engineering
docs or agent rules yet. Python's stdlib script accepts one name and prints a greeting.
No tests, installs, package distribution, translations or API exist yet.

## Task for an independently scoped executor

Receive **only the finished pack and this project**, copied to an owned disposable
workspace. Use the appropriate skill to bootstrap sufficient engineering docs.
Before writing list finite paths; use facts above, inspect the tiny script, and mark
unknown product decisions as assumptions/draft. Do not invent a test command.
A stdlib CLI smoke is permitted on a synthetic name if the assigned executor has
that authority; only an actually run command may be called verified.

Then demonstrate:
1. Propose a substantial *future* `--uppercase` option: user/scenario, failure and
   boundary, minimal plan and verification criteria. Do not implement the feature
   or call its proposal an implemented capability.
2. A punctuation-only documentation fix must not create an architecture programme.
3. Reapply bootstrap with no changed need. Record whether any delta is justified;
   no duplicate docs or loss of manual rules. A hash comparison can witness bytes,
   but does not replace the executor's decision/procedure evidence.

Expected witnesses: chosen skill/resources and their actual paths; finite initial
and second-pass changed paths; primary owners/navigation; assumptions separated
from facts; actual commands/exits or NOT_RUN; short output and concrete remainder.
No GUI or external service is needed.
